questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं :
कथन I : विश्व बैंक की स्थापना द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के बाद वर्ष 1945 में हुई थी ।
कथन II : विश्व बैंक की गतिविधियों का ध्यान विकासशील देशों पर केंद्रित है ।
उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The World Bank was created after the Second World War in the year 1945.
Statement II : The activities of the World Bank are focused on the developing countries.
In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.A: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं ।
options.B: कथन I और कथन II दोनों असत्य हैं ।
options.C: कथन I सत्य है, परंतु कथन II असत्य है ।
options.D: कथन I असत्य है, परंतु कथन II सत्य है ।

options_english.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options_english.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
options_english.C: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false.
options_english.D: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true.

questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The World Bank was indeed established in 1945 following the Bretton Woods Conference held in 1944, as part of the post-World War II international economic order. Statement II is also true because the World Bank primarily focuses its lending and development activities on developing countries, providing financial and technical assistance to reduce poverty and promote sustainable development. Options B, C, and D are incorrect as they incorrectly characterise the truth value of one or both statements.
questions.solution_hindi: दोनों कथन सही हैं। विश्व बैंक की स्थापना 1945 में ब्रेटन वुड्स सम्मेलन (1944) के बाद द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के पश्चात हुई थी। कथन II भी सही है क्योंकि विश्व बैंक मुख्य रूप से अपनी ऋण एवं विकास गतिविधियाँ विकासशील देशों पर केंद्रित करता है, जिससे गरीबी कम हो और सतत विकास हो सके।

questions.text: 'क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल' का मुख्य उद्देश्य निम्नलिखित में से क्या था ?
questions.text_english: The major objective of 'Kyoto Protocol' was :

options.A: ग्रीनहाउस गैसों के उत्सर्जन को कम करना ।
options.B: प्रदूषण को कम करने के लिए वन आवरण को बढ़ाना ।
options.C: पर्यावरण प्रदूषण को नियंत्रित करने के लिए विकासशील देशों को अनुदान-सहायता प्रदान करना ।

options_english.B: to reduce pollution by increasing forest cover.
options_english.C: to provide grant-in-aid to the developing nations to control environmental pollution.

questions.solution: The primary objective of the Kyoto Protocol (1997) was to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, making option A correct. The protocol legally bound developed countries to emission reduction targets, recognising these gases as the principal drivers of climate change. Option B is incorrect because increasing forest cover, while beneficial, was not the protocol's stated objective. Option C is incorrect as the protocol did not primarily deal with grants to developing nations. Option D (sustainable development) is a broader concept and not the specific focus of the Kyoto Protocol.
questions.solution_hindi: क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल (1997) का मुख्य उद्देश्य ग्रीनहाउस गैसों के उत्सर्जन को कम करना था। इस प्रोटोकॉल ने विकसित देशों को उत्सर्जन कटौती के लक्ष्य कानूनी रूप से बाध्यकारी बनाए। शेष विकल्प इसके वास्तविक उद्देश्य से मेल नहीं खाते।

questions.text: 'सतत विकास' की अवधारणा निम्नलिखित में से किस एक पर जोर देती है ?
questions.text_english: The concept of 'sustainable development' emphasises on :

options.A: मानव विकास के लिए संसाधनों का अधिकतम उपयोग करना
options.B: किसी देश के सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (जीडीपी) को बढ़ाना
options.C: आर्थिक विकास को पारिस्थितिक उत्तरदायित्व से जोड़ना
options.D: पर्यावरण संरक्षण के लिए किए जाने वाले प्रयासों में वृद्धि करना

options_english.A: utilizing maximum resources for human development.
options_english.B: increasing Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a country.
options_english.C: combining economic growth with ecological responsibility.
options_english.D: maximising the efforts for environmental conservation.

questions.solution: The concept of sustainable development, as popularised by the Brundtland Commission Report (1987), emphasises combining economic growth with ecological responsibility, making option C correct. It stresses meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. Option A is incorrect because sustainable development discourages maximum or unchecked exploitation of resources. Option B is too narrow as GDP growth alone ignores environmental costs. Option D focuses only on conservation without the developmental aspect, which is also incomplete.
questions.solution_hindi: सतत विकास की अवधारणा (ब्रंटलैंड आयोग, 1987) आर्थिक विकास को पारिस्थितिक उत्तरदायित्व से जोड़ने पर जोर देती है। इसका अर्थ है वर्तमान पीढ़ी की जरूरतें पूरी करते हुए भविष्य की पीढ़ियों की जरूरतों से समझौता न करना। विकल्प C सबसे उचित है।

questions.text:
सूची-I में दिए गए राज्यों का सूची-II में दिए गए उन राज्यों से सही मिलान कीजिए जिनसे अलग करके इन्हें बनाया गया था । नीचे दिए गए कूट से सही उत्तर चुनिए :
सूची-I : 1. गुजरात, 2. हरियाणा, 3. मेघालय, 4. छत्तीसगढ़
सूची-II : (i) असम, (ii) बॉम्बे, (iii) मध्य प्रदेश, (iv) पंजाब
questions.text_english:
Match the States given in List-I with the States from which these were carved out given in List-II correctly. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below :
List-I : 1. Gujarat, 2. Haryana, 3. Meghalaya, 4. Chhattisgarh
List-II : (i) Assam, (ii) Bombay, (iii) Madhya Pradesh, (iv) Punjab
questions.solution: The correct matching is option B: Gujarat was carved out of Bombay state in 1960; Haryana was carved out of Punjab in 1966; Meghalaya was carved out of Assam in 1972; and Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000. All other options incorrectly pair one or more states with wrong parent states. This correct pairing reflects the linguistic and administrative reorganisation of Indian states in the post-independence era.
questions.solution_hindi: सही मिलान विकल्प B है: गुजरात को 1960 में बॉम्बे से, हरियाणा को 1966 में पंजाब से, मेघालय को 1972 में असम से, और छत्तीसगढ़ को 2000 में मध्य प्रदेश से अलग करके बनाया गया था। अन्य विकल्प गलत युग्म प्रस्तुत करते हैं।

questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं, जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) के रूप में अंकित किया गया है । इन कथनों को पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए :
अभिकथन (A) : यूरोपीय संघ का अपना ध्वज, राष्ट्रगान, अपनी स्थापना तिथि और मुद्रा है।
कारण (R) : समकालीन विश्व में यूरोपीय संघ का आर्थिक, राजनीतिक और सैन्य क्षेत्रों में बहुत प्रभाव है ।
questions.text_english:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R). Read these statements and choose the correct answer from the given below options :
Assertion (A) : The European Union has its own flag, anthem, founding date and currency.
Reason (R) : The European Union has a major influence on the economic, political and military fields in the contemporary world.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है ।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: Option B is correct. Both the Assertion and the Reason are individually true statements. The EU does possess its own flag, anthem, founding date (1 November 1993 when the Maastricht Treaty came into force), and currency (the Euro). The EU also has considerable economic, political, and to a degree military influence globally. However, the Reason does not explain the Assertion — the EU having its own symbols is not because of its global influence; rather, the symbols reflect its supranational institutional identity. Hence, while both statements are true, the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
questions.solution_hindi: विकल्प B सही है। अभिकथन (A) सत्य है क्योंकि यूरोपीय संघ का अपना ध्वज, राष्ट्रगान, स्थापना तिथि और यूरो मुद्रा है। कारण (R) भी सत्य है क्योंकि EU का वैश्विक स्तर पर आर्थिक व राजनीतिक प्रभाव है। परंतु कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता क्योंकि EU के प्रतीक उसके वैश्विक प्रभाव के कारण नहीं, बल्कि उसकी अतिराष्ट्रीय पहचान के प्रतीक हैं।

questions.text: 1953 में राज्य पुनर्गठन आयोग को किस लिए नियुक्त किया गया था ?
questions.text_english: The States Reorganisation Commission was appointed in 1953 :

options.A: प्रशासनिक कार्यकुशलता को सुनिश्चित करने के लिए
options.B: औपनिवेशिक शासन के दौरान निर्धारित प्रांतों की सीमाओं से संबंधित जटिलताओं को समाप्त करने के लिए
options.C: राष्ट्र निर्माण की प्रक्रिया को सुनिश्चित करने के लिए
options.D: भाषा के आधार पर राज्यों की सीमाओं का सीमांकन करने के लिए

options_english.B: to end complexities regarding demarcation of the provinces' boundaries during colonial rule.
options_english.C: to ensure process of nation building.
options_english.D: for demarcation of states' boundaries on the basis of language.

questions.solution: The States Reorganisation Commission was appointed in 1953 primarily for the demarcation of states' boundaries on the basis of language, making option D correct. This was a response to strong popular demands, particularly from Telugu-speaking people in the Andhra region, who demanded a separate linguistic state. The commission's report led to the States Reorganisation Act of 1956, which reorganised state boundaries largely along linguistic lines. Options A, B, and C describe related but secondary considerations and are not the primary stated purpose of the commission.
questions.solution_hindi: राज्य पुनर्गठन आयोग को 1953 में मुख्यतः भाषाई आधार पर राज्यों की सीमाओं का सीमांकन करने के लिए नियुक्त किया गया था। आंध्र प्रदेश के तेलुगुभाषी लोगों के आंदोलन के बाद यह आवश्यक हो गया था। इसकी रिपोर्ट के आधार पर 1956 का राज्य पुनर्गठन अधिनियम बनाया गया।

questions.text: संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद में भारत की स्थायी सदस्यता से संबंधित दावेदारी के समर्थन के लिए निम्नलिखित में से सर्वश्रेष्ठ तर्क को चुनिए :
questions.text_english: Choose the best argument to support India's claim for permanent membership in the United Nations Security Council :

options.A: भारत की बढ़ती आर्थिक शक्ति और स्थिर राजनीतिक व्यवस्था
options.C: भारत की संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ में इसकी स्थापना से ही सदस्यता
options.D: भारत का संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ के बजट में योगदान देने वाला सदस्य देश होना

options_english.A: India's growing economic power and stable political system
options_english.C: India's membership in the United Nations Organization since its inception
options_english.D: India as the contributing member country in the United Nations Organisation's budget

questions.solution: The strongest argument supporting India's claim for a permanent seat in the UN Security Council is its growing economic power and stable political system, making option A correct. India is one of the world's largest economies, a nuclear state, the world's most populous democracy, and a significant contributor to UN peacekeeping missions — all of which establish a credible basis for permanent membership. Option B (effective leadership) is subjective. Option C (founding membership) applies to many countries. Option D (budget contribution) is a weak standalone argument as many countries contribute financially without claiming permanent membership.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत की बढ़ती आर्थिक शक्ति और स्थिर राजनीतिक व्यवस्था सबसे मजबूत तर्क है। भारत विश्व की सबसे बड़ी लोकतांत्रिक व परमाणु शक्ति है, UN शांति अभियानों में अग्रणी योगदानकर्ता है और एक उभरती वैश्विक शक्ति है। यही कारण है कि विकल्प A सबसे उचित तर्क है।

निम्नलिखित घटनाओं को कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए :
(i) चीन द्वारा परमाणु परीक्षण करना
(ii) भारत द्वारा प्रथम परमाणु विस्फोट करना
(iii) परमाणु अप्रसार संधि का लागू होना
(iv) भारत में होमी जहाँगीर भाभा के निदेशन में परमाणु कार्यक्रम को प्रारंभ किया जाना

questions.text_english:
Arrange the following events in a chronological order :
(i) Atomic test conducted by China
(ii) First nuclear explosion conducted by India
(iii) Implementation of Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
(iv) Initiation of the atomic programme in India under the guidance of Homi Jehangir Bhabha
Choose the correct option :
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is option B: (iv) India's atomic programme was initiated under Homi Jehangir Bhabha in 1948; (i) China conducted its first atomic test in 1964; (iii) the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) came into force in 1970; and (ii) India conducted its first nuclear explosion (Pokhran-I) in 1974. All other options place these events in an incorrect sequence. This order reflects the progressive development of India's nuclear programme against the backdrop of global nuclear proliferation.
questions.solution_hindi: सही कालक्रम विकल्प B है: (iv) भारत में 1948 में भाभा के नेतृत्व में परमाणु कार्यक्रम प्रारंभ; (i) 1964 में चीन का परमाणु परीक्षण; (iii) 1970 में परमाणु अप्रसार संधि लागू; (ii) 1974 में भारत का पोखरण-I परमाणु विस्फोट। यही सही क्रम है।

questions.text: कौन-से वर्ष भारत के सबसे बड़े सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के उद्यम रेलवे ने हड़ताल की थी ?
questions.text_english: In which year did the largest public sector undertaking, Railways, go on a strike ?
questions.solution: The historic railway strike took place in 1974, making option A correct. Led by George Fernandes, the railway workers went on a nationwide strike demanding better wages and service conditions. It was the largest industrial strike in independent India's history, involving around 17 lakh workers. The government under Indira Gandhi dealt with the strike firmly. This event became one of the contributing factors to the political turmoil that eventually led to the imposition of Emergency in 1975.
questions.solution_hindi: 1974 में जॉर्ज फर्नांडीस के नेतृत्व में रेलवे कर्मचारियों ने राष्ट्रव्यापी हड़ताल की थी। यह स्वतंत्र भारत की सबसे बड़ी औद्योगिक हड़ताल थी जिसमें लगभग 17 लाख कर्मचारी शामिल थे। इंदिरा गांधी सरकार ने इसे सख्ती से दबाया था।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा निर्णय 24 जून, 1975 को सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने इंदिरा गांधी के केस के मामले में दिया था ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following was the decision of the Supreme Court given on 24 June, 1975 about the Indira Gandhi case ?

options.A: इंदिरा गांधी का निर्वाचन अवैधानिक था ।
options.B: इंदिरा गांधी ने संविधान के 'बुनियादी ढाँचे' की अवधारणा के खिलाफ अपने चुनाव अभियान में सरकारी कर्मचारियों की सेवाओं का उपयोग किया ।
options.C: इंदिरा गांधी को तुरंत अपने पद से त्याग-पत्र देने का आदेश दिया गया ।
options.D: इंदिरा गांधी के मामले में उच्च न्यायालय द्वारा दिए गए फैसले पर आंशिक स्थगनादेश सुनाया गया, जिससे वह संसद सदस्य बनी रहेंगी, परंतु लोक सभा की कार्यवाहियों में भाग नहीं ले पाएंगी ।

options_english.A: Election of Indira Gandhi was invalid.
options_english.B: Indira Gandhi used the services of the government officials in her election campaign which is against the concept of 'basic structure' of the Constitution.
options_english.C: Indira Gandhi was ordered to resign from her post immediately.
options_english.D: Indira Gandhi was granted a partial stay on the High Court order, allowing her to remain a member of the Parliament, but could not take part in the Lok Sabha proceedings.

questions.solution: On 24 June 1975, the Supreme Court granted a partial conditional stay on the Allahabad High Court's order, making option D correct. The High Court had found Indira Gandhi guilty of electoral malpractice. The Supreme Court's stay allowed her to remain a Member of Parliament but barred her from participating in Lok Sabha proceedings or voting. Option A is incorrect because the High Court, not the Supreme Court, declared her election invalid. Option B incorrectly references the 'basic structure' doctrine. Option C is incorrect as she was not ordered to resign immediately.
questions.solution_hindi: 24 जून 1975 को सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने इंदिरा गांधी के मामले में इलाहाबाद उच्च न्यायालय के फैसले पर आंशिक स्थगनादेश दिया। इससे वह संसद सदस्य बनी रह सकती थीं परंतु लोक सभा की कार्यवाहियों में भाग नहीं ले सकती थीं। यह निर्णय आपातकाल घोषणा की पृष्ठभूमि बना।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा देश आसियान का संस्थापक नहीं था ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following countries was not a founder of ASEAN ?
questions.solution: China was not a founding member of ASEAN, making option C correct. ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) was established on 8 August 1967 by five founding members: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand. China is not a member of ASEAN at all — it participates in related forums like the ASEAN+3 dialogue. Options A (Singapore), B (Indonesia), and D (Thailand) are all original founding members and are therefore incorrect answers to this question.
questions.solution_hindi: चीन आसियान का संस्थापक सदस्य नहीं था। आसियान (दक्षिण-पूर्व एशियाई राष्ट्रों का संघ) की स्थापना 8 अगस्त 1967 को इंडोनेशिया, मलेशिया, फिलीपींस, सिंगापुर और थाईलैंड ने मिलकर की थी। चीन आसियान का सदस्य भी नहीं है।

questions.text: गुट-निरपेक्ष आंदोलन (NAM) का पहला सम्मेलन किस शहर में हुआ था ?
questions.text_english: In which city was the first Summit of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) held ?
questions.solution: The first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement was held in Belgrade (Yugoslavia) in 1961, making option A correct. It was attended by 25 heads of state and hosted by Yugoslav President Josip Broz Tito. Bandung (option B) was the site of the Afro-Asian Conference of 1955 which laid the groundwork for NAM but was not a NAM summit itself. Tokyo and Delhi were never sites of the first NAM summit.
questions.solution_hindi: गुट-निरपेक्ष आंदोलन (NAM) का पहला सम्मेलन 1961 में बेलग्रेड (यूगोस्लाविया) में हुआ था। इसमें 25 राष्ट्राध्यक्षों ने भाग लिया था। बांडुंग 1955 के अफ्रो-एशियाई सम्मेलन का स्थान था जिसने NAM की नींव रखी, परंतु वह NAM का सम्मेलन नहीं था।

questions.text: सोवियत संघ के किन्हीं चार गणराज्यों के नाम लिखिए ।
questions.text_english: Name any four republics of the Soviet Union.

key_points: Russia (Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic)
Ukraine (Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic)
Kazakhstan (Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic)
Belarus / Georgia / Armenia / Azerbaijan / Uzbekistan / Tajikistan / Turkmenistan / Kyrgyzstan / Moldova / Latvia / Lithuania / Estonia (any one more)

questions.solution: The Soviet Union was composed of fifteen republics. Any four of the following may be named: Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia. These republics declared independence one by one between 1990 and 1991, leading to the formal dissolution of the Soviet Union in December 1991.
questions.solution_hindi: सोवियत संघ 15 गणराज्यों से मिलकर बना था। इनमें से किन्हीं चार के नाम इस प्रकार हैं: (1) रूस, (2) यूक्रेन, (3) कजाकिस्तान, (4) बेलारूस। इन सभी गणराज्यों ने 1990-91 के बीच स्वतंत्रता की घोषणा की और दिसंबर 1991 में सोवियत संघ का विघटन हो गया।

questions.text: "कुछ समूहों द्वारा वैश्वीकरण का विरोध किए जाने के बावजूद भी यह भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए वरदान साबित हुआ है।" इस कथन की पुष्टि कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: "Globalization has been a boon for the economy of India despite the resistance shown by certain groups." Support the statement.

key_points: Globalization brought foreign direct investment (FDI) leading to industrial growth
IT and service sector boom — India became a global IT hub
Rise in exports and GDP growth, increased employment opportunities

questions.solution: Globalisation has indeed proved to be a boon for India's economy. Since liberalisation in 1991, foreign direct investment has poured into multiple sectors, boosting industrial output and infrastructure. India emerged as a global information technology and services hub, with companies like Infosys and TCS gaining worldwide recognition. Exports expanded significantly, raising GDP and creating millions of jobs in sectors like software, pharmaceuticals, and textiles. Though some groups — such as small farmers and traditional industries — faced challenges, the overall economic gains far outweighed the resistance.
questions.solution_hindi: वैश्वीकरण भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए वरदान साबित हुआ है। 1991 की उदारीकरण नीति के बाद विदेशी प्रत्यक्ष निवेश बढ़ा, भारत एक वैश्विक IT केंद्र बना, निर्यात में वृद्धि हुई और लाखों लोगों को रोजगार मिला। सॉफ्टवेयर, फार्मास्यूटिकल्स और वस्त्र उद्योग में भारत की वैश्विक पहचान बनी।

questions.topic: वैश्वीकरण और भारत / Globalisation and India

questions.text: प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना और द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना के मध्य किन्हीं दो मूलभूत अंतरों को उजागर कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Highlight any two fundamental differences between the First Five Year Plan and the Second Five Year Plan.

key_points: First Plan prioritised agriculture and irrigation; Second Plan emphasised heavy industry and rapid industrialisation
First Plan was cautious and consolidating; Second Plan was ambitious and based on the Mahalanobis model of rapid socialist-pattern development

questions.solution: The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) focused primarily on agriculture, land reforms, and irrigation, as India had just emerged from Partition and needed food security. In contrast, the Second Five Year Plan (1956-61), based on the Mahalanobis model, emphasised rapid industrialisation with heavy investment in public sector steel, mining, and machine-building industries. The first plan was cautious and consolidatory in nature, while the second was ambitious and aimed at transforming India into a socialist industrial economy.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना (1951-56) का ध्यान कृषि, भूमि सुधार और सिंचाई पर था। द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना (1956-61) महालनोबिस मॉडल पर आधारित थी और भारी उद्योगों, इस्पात संयंत्रों तथा सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र की स्थापना पर बल देती थी। पहली योजना संतुलित थी, दूसरी महत्त्वाकांक्षी और औद्योगीकरण-केंद्रित।

questions.text: 1975 में राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल घोषित करने के लिए तत्कालीन सरकार ने कौन-से दो कारण दिए थे ?
questions.text_english: Which two reasons were given by the Government for declaring the National Emergency in 1975 ?

key_points: Internal disturbances and threat to internal security — opposition movements like JP Movement were destabilising governance
External threat / threat to the unity and integrity of India (official justification under Article 352)

questions.solution: The government headed by Indira Gandhi declared the National Emergency on 25 June 1975, citing two main reasons. First, there was a threat to internal security due to widespread agitation led by Jayaprakash Narayan's movement, strikes, and political instability, which the government claimed was destabilising the country. Second, the government cited an external threat to India's sovereignty and integrity as the official constitutional justification under Article 352. Critics, however, argued that these reasons were used to suppress legitimate democratic opposition.
questions.solution_hindi: इंदिरा गांधी सरकार ने 25 जून 1975 को राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल घोषित किया। इसके दो आधिकारिक कारण दिए गए: पहला, जयप्रकाश नारायण के आंदोलन, हड़तालों और राजनीतिक अस्थिरता के कारण आंतरिक सुरक्षा को खतरा; दूसरा, अनुच्छेद 352 के अंतर्गत भारत की एकता और अखंडता को बाहरी खतरे का हवाला। आलोचकों ने इसे विपक्ष को दबाने का तरीका बताया।

questions.text: विश्व में वैश्वीकरण को तीव्रता से बढ़ावा देने में सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी किस प्रकार उत्तरदायी है ? दो उदाहरणों से स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: How has Information Technology been responsible in accelerating globalization across the world ? Explain with two examples.

key_points: Internet and digital communication have eliminated geographical barriers, enabling instant global transactions and communication
E-commerce and outsourcing enabled by IT have integrated national economies into a global marketplace

questions.solution: Information Technology has been a powerful driver of globalisation by eliminating barriers of time and distance. First, the internet and digital communication platforms allow businesses, governments, and individuals to share information, conduct trade, and communicate instantaneously across the globe — for instance, Indian IT companies like Infosys provide software services to American clients in real time. Second, e-commerce platforms such as Amazon and Flipkart have created borderless marketplaces, allowing consumers in one country to buy goods from sellers in another, integrating national economies seamlessly.
questions.solution_hindi: सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी ने समय और दूरी की बाधाओं को समाप्त करके वैश्वीकरण को तीव्र किया है। पहला उदाहरण: इंटरनेट और डिजिटल संचार के माध्यम से भारतीय IT कंपनियाँ जैसे इन्फोसिस अमेरिकी ग्राहकों को वास्तविक समय में सेवाएँ प्रदान करती हैं। दूसरा उदाहरण: Amazon और Flipkart जैसी ई-कॉमर्स कंपनियाँ राष्ट्रीय अर्थव्यवस्थाओं को एकीकृत करते हुए वैश्विक बाजार बना रही हैं।

questions.text: 2014 के आम चुनाव के बाद केंद्र की गठबंधन सरकारों के स्वरूप में आए परिवर्तन के लिए उत्तरदायी किन्हीं दो कारकों का विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Analyse any two factors responsible for the change in the nature of coalition governments at the Centre after the General Elections of 2014.

key_points: BJP won an absolute majority on its own in 2014, ending the era of compulsory coalition dependency
Strong leadership and centralised campaign reduced the bargaining power of regional parties

questions.solution: After the 2014 General Elections, the nature of coalition governments at the Centre changed significantly. First, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) secured an absolute majority on its own with 282 seats in the Lok Sabha, marking a shift from the fragmented mandates of 1989-2014 when no single party could govern without relying heavily on regional parties. Second, the strong leadership of Narendra Modi and a presidential-style campaign reduced regional parties' bargaining power, transforming coalition politics from a compulsion to a managed arrangement where allies had limited influence on policy decisions.
questions.solution_hindi: 2014 के आम चुनावों के बाद गठबंधन सरकारों का स्वरूप बदल गया। पहला कारण: BJP ने 282 सीटें जीतकर अपने दम पर पूर्ण बहुमत प्राप्त किया, जिससे क्षेत्रीय दलों पर निर्भरता समाप्त हुई। दूसरा कारण: नरेंद्र मोदी के मजबूत नेतृत्व और राष्ट्रीय स्तर के चुनाव प्रचार ने क्षेत्रीय दलों की सौदेबाजी शक्ति को कम कर दिया।

questions.text: औपनिवेशिक शासन की समाप्ति के पश्चात् भाषा के आधार पर राज्यों के पुनर्गठन से संबंधित भारत सरकार की किन्हीं दो मुख्य चिंताओं की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain any two major concerns of Indian government regarding the reorganisation of states on the basis of language after the end of colonial rule.

key_points: Fear that linguistic reorganisation would strengthen regional identities at the cost of national unity and lead to balkanisation
Concern that it would reignite communal and ethnic tensions, making administration more complex
Worry that it might set a precedent leading to endless fragmentation of states

questions.solution: After independence, the Indian government had serious reservations about reorganising states on a linguistic basis, fearing that it could undermine national unity and territorial integrity. The first major concern was that linguistic reorganisation might encourage narrow regionalism and separatist tendencies. Leaders like Jawaharlal Nehru and Sardar Patel feared that if states were formed on the basis of language, people might develop stronger loyalties towards their linguistic group than towards the Indian nation as a whole, potentially threatening the fragile unity of newly independent India. The second major concern was that linguistic reorganisation could open a Pandora's box, with every linguistic community demanding a separate state. This would lead to endless fragmentation of the country. The government feared that once language became the basis for state formation, other communities would use religion, caste, or ethnicity as similar grounds, making governance increasingly complex and divisive.
questions.solution_hindi: स्वतंत्रता के बाद भारत सरकार को भाषाई आधार पर राज्यों के पुनर्गठन को लेकर दो प्रमुख चिंताएँ थीं। पहली चिंता यह थी कि भाषाई पुनर्गठन से संकीर्ण क्षेत्रीयवाद और अलगाववादी प्रवृत्तियाँ बढ़ सकती हैं। नेहरू और पटेल को डर था कि लोग राष्ट्र से अधिक अपनी भाषाई पहचान को प्राथमिकता देने लगेंगे, जिससे नवजात राष्ट्र की एकता को खतरा होगा। दूसरी चिंता यह थी कि यदि भाषा राज्य निर्माण का आधार बन गई, तो अन्य समुदाय भी जाति, धर्म या नस्ल के आधार पर अलग राज्यों की मांग करेंगे। इससे देश का अनंत विभाजन होता रहेगा और शासन जटिल हो जाएगा।

questions.text: सोवियत संघ के विघटन के बाद शॉक थेरेपी के किन्हीं चार प्रभावों को उजागर कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Highlight any four effects of the shock therapy after the disintegration of the Soviet Union.

key_points: Collapse of entire industries and mass unemployment
Ruble became worthless, causing hyperinflation and economic hardship
Privatisation led to 'crony capitalism' — state assets grabbed by oligarchs
Poverty, food insecurity, and collapse of social welfare systems

questions.solution: Shock therapy, the rapid transition from a communist command economy to a capitalist free-market economy, had devastating effects on the post-Soviet states. First, it led to the complete collapse of entire industries and resulted in massive unemployment, as state-owned enterprises were suddenly shut down without alternative employment opportunities. Second, the ruble (Russia's currency) lost almost all its value, leading to severe hyperinflation. The savings of ordinary citizens were wiped out overnight, pushing millions into poverty. Third, the privatisation process was deeply flawed. State assets were sold off cheaply or manipulated by a small group of politically connected businessmen, creating a class of oligarchs who controlled much of the national wealth, a phenomenon often called 'crony capitalism.' Fourth, the welfare systems that had guaranteed free healthcare, education, and subsidised food under the Soviet system collapsed, leading to widespread food insecurity, health crises, and social breakdown, particularly affecting the elderly and marginalised communities.
questions.solution_hindi: शॉक थेरेपी के चार प्रमुख प्रभाव निम्नलिखित थे: पहला, अनेक उद्योगों का पतन हो गया और बड़े पैमाने पर बेरोजगारी फैल गई क्योंकि सरकारी उपक्रम अचानक बंद कर दिए गए। दूसरा, रूबल की कीमत लगभग शून्य हो गई और भारी मुद्रास्फीति ने आम नागरिकों की जमा-पूंजी समाप्त कर दी। तीसरा, निजीकरण प्रक्रिया में गड़बड़ी के कारण 'ओलिगार्क' वर्ग का उदय हुआ जिसने सरकारी संपत्तियाँ सस्ते दामों पर हासिल कर लीं। चौथा, सोवियत काल की कल्याणकारी व्यवस्था — मुफ्त शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य और सब्सिडीयुक्त भोजन — ध्वस्त हो गई, जिससे गरीबी और सामाजिक संकट बढ़ा।

questions.text_english: Analyse any two major challenges faced by the Election Commission before conducting the first General Elections in India after independence.

key_points: Preparing an electoral roll for a vast, largely illiterate population with no previous democratic experience at this scale
Managing elections across diverse geography with limited infrastructure and communication

questions.solution: The first General Elections of 1951-52 were a monumental undertaking, and the Election Commission faced several formidable challenges. The first major challenge was preparing the electoral rolls for a massive and largely illiterate population. India had about 36 crore citizens, the majority of whom could neither read nor write. Registering all eligible voters, ensuring accuracy, and dealing with widespread name duplication and errors was an enormous administrative challenge that had never been attempted at this scale anywhere in the world. The second major challenge was conducting free and fair elections across a geographically vast and infrastructurally underdeveloped country. Polling booths had to be set up in remote villages, mountains, deserts, and forests. Communication systems were poor, transportation was limited, and trained polling personnel were scarce. Despite all these difficulties, the Election Commission under Sukumar Sen successfully conducted the elections, establishing India as a credible democracy.

sub_questions.text_english: "The United Nations Organisation is generally regarded as the great hope of humanity for peace and progress." Support the statement with two arguments.

key_points: UN has played a crucial role in maintaining international peace through peacekeeping missions and conflict resolution
UN agencies like UNICEF, WHO, UNESCO have promoted human development, health, education, and humanitarian assistance globally

sub_questions.solution: The United Nations Organisation is rightly regarded as the great hope of humanity for peace and progress. The first argument in support of this is the UN's role in maintaining international peace and security. Through its peacekeeping missions, the UN has deployed troops to conflict zones across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, successfully preventing the escalation of several regional conflicts. The Security Council serves as the primary platform for resolving disputes through diplomacy rather than warfare. The second argument pertains to the UN's role in global development and humanitarian assistance. Agencies such as UNICEF (child welfare), WHO (global health), UNESCO (education and culture), and the UNDP (development) have collectively worked to eradicate poverty, combat diseases, promote literacy, and provide emergency relief to millions of people affected by wars and natural disasters. These efforts make the UN an indispensable institution for human progress.

sub_questions.text_english: Suggest any four measures to make the United Nations Organisation more relevant in the current scenario.

key_points: Reform the Security Council to include more permanent members representing developing nations
Strengthen the UN's financial base by ensuring regular and equitable contributions from all member states
Empower the UN General Assembly to have more binding authority in international disputes
Enhance the UN's capacity to address non-traditional security threats like terrorism, climate change, and pandemics

sub_questions.solution: To make the United Nations more relevant in the contemporary world, several reforms are essential. First, the Security Council must be reformed and expanded to include permanent or semi-permanent members from developing regions like Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Countries such as India, Brazil, and South Africa have strong claims. The current structure reflecting post-World War II power is outdated. Second, the UN's financial independence must be strengthened by ensuring that all member states pay their contributions on time and in full, reducing dependence on a few powerful donors. Third, the General Assembly should be given greater decision-making authority so that resolutions on global issues carry binding weight rather than being merely advisory. Fourth, the UN must enhance its capacity to address non-traditional security threats such as terrorism, climate change, global pandemics, and cybersecurity, which are the defining challenges of the 21st century and require coordinated multilateral responses.

sub_questions.text_english: Why have the global efforts to protect the environment not been as successful as desired ? Analyse the reasons.

key_points: Conflict between economic development priorities and environmental protection
USA's withdrawal from Kyoto Protocol weakened global commitment
Disagreement between developed and developing nations over responsibility
Lack of binding enforcement mechanisms in international environmental agreements

sub_questions.solution: Despite numerous global conferences and agreements, efforts to protect the environment have not yielded the desired results due to several interconnected reasons. First, there is a fundamental conflict between economic growth and environmental protection. Developing nations prioritise industrialisation and poverty elimination, arguing that curbing their emissions would impede development. Developed nations, on the other hand, are reluctant to drastically reduce their consumption-based emissions. Second, the withdrawal of the United States from the Kyoto Protocol seriously undermined global commitment to emission reduction, as the US is historically the world's largest emitter. Third, the dispute over the 'common but differentiated responsibilities' principle — whether developed nations should bear greater responsibility than developing ones — has created a persistent deadlock in climate negotiations. Fourth, most international environmental agreements lack strong enforcement mechanisms, meaning countries can violate targets without real consequences, rendering treaties largely aspirational rather than legally binding.

sub_questions.text_english: Evaluate the efforts made to achieve the objectives of the Rio Declaration by the developed and developing countries.

key_points: Developed countries pledged financial and technological assistance to developing nations but largely failed to meet targets
Developing countries committed to sustainable development but faced tension between growth and conservation
Rio led to Agenda 21, UNFCCC and Convention on Biodiversity — significant institutional achievements
Implementation gaps remain wide due to economic interests overriding environmental commitments

sub_questions.solution: The 1992 Rio Declaration (Earth Summit) set ambitious objectives around sustainable development, biodiversity, and climate change. The efforts of both developed and developing nations in achieving these objectives present a mixed picture. Developed countries pledged to provide financial resources and transfer environmentally sound technologies to developing nations. Some progress was made through mechanisms like the Global Environment Facility. However, most developed nations failed to meet their promised 0.7% of GDP contribution for environmental aid, and technology transfer remained limited due to intellectual property concerns. Developing countries committed to sustainable development and signed the Convention on Biological Diversity and the UNFCCC. However, rapid economic growth pressures led many to prioritise industrial expansion over conservation. China and India, for instance, significantly increased their emissions in the decades after Rio. Overall, while the Rio Declaration created significant institutional frameworks like Agenda 21, the gap between commitments and actual implementation has remained wide, reflecting the primacy of national economic interests over global environmental responsibility.

questions.text_english:
Read the passage given below carefully and answer the questions based on it :

India made earnest efforts for the early realisation of freedom of Indonesia from the Dutch colonial regime by convening an international conference in 1949 to support its freedom struggle. India was a staunch supporter of the decolonisation process and firmly opposed racism, especially apartheid in South Africa. The Afro-Asian Conference held in the Indonesian city of Bandung in 1955, commonly known as the Bandung Conference, marked the zenith of India's engagement with the newly independent Asian and African nations. The Bandung Conference later led to the establishment of the NAM.

sub_questions.text: एफ्रो-एशियाई एकता को साकार करने में किस भारतीय नेता ने महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई थी ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which Indian leader played an important role in manifesting the Afro-Asian unity ?
sub_questions.solution: Jawaharlal Nehru played the most important role in manifesting Afro-Asian unity. As India's first Prime Minister, Nehru championed anti-colonialism, decolonisation, and solidarity among newly independent nations. He was a key organiser of the 1949 international conference supporting Indonesia and a leading figure at the 1955 Bandung Conference. His foreign policy vision of Panchsheel and non-alignment shaped the Afro-Asian solidarity movement.

sub_questions.text: एफ्रो-एशियाई एकता किस वर्ष गुट-निरपेक्ष आंदोलन का प्रतीक बन गई ?
sub_questions.text_english: In which year did the Non-Alignment Movement become the symbol of Afro-Asian unity ?
sub_questions.solution: The Non-Aligned Movement formally became the symbol of Afro-Asian unity in 1961, when the first NAM summit was held in Belgrade, Yugoslavia. Twenty-five nations participated, most of which were newly independent Afro-Asian countries. This summit formalised the movement that had been building since the 1955 Bandung Conference, representing the collective voice of nations refusing to align with either the American or Soviet blocs during the Cold War.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the main intention behind the strengthening Afro-Asian unity.

options.A: अमरीकी खेमे से आर्थिक सहायता प्राप्त करना
options.B: सोवियत संघ गुट को उसकी वैश्विक नीतियों को बढ़ावा देने में सहयोग करना
options.C: शीत युद्ध के दौर में सैन्य गठबंधन का निर्माण करना
options.D: अपनी स्वतंत्रता को बनाए रखने के लिए दोनों महाशक्तियों (अमरीका व सोवियत संघ) से दूरी बनाए रखना

options_english.A: To gain economic support from the USA bloc
options_english.B: To co-operate with the USSR bloc in enhancing its global policies
options_english.C: To form military alliances in the era of Cold War
options_english.D: To maintain distance from both the superpowers (USA and USSR) in order to protect its freedom

sub_questions.solution: The main intention behind strengthening Afro-Asian unity was to maintain independence from both Cold War superpowers — the USA and the USSR — in order to protect the newly won freedom of these nations. The newly independent countries of Africa and Asia feared that aligning with either superpower bloc would compromise their sovereignty and draw them into Cold War conflicts. By standing together and refusing alignment, they sought to chart an independent foreign policy path.

sub_questions.text: गुट-निरपेक्ष आंदोलन (NAM) का पहला सम्मेलन किस वर्ष में हुआ था ?
sub_questions.text_english: The first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) was held in which year ?
sub_questions.solution: The first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement was held in 1961 in Belgrade, Yugoslavia. It was attended by 25 nations and was co-hosted by leaders including Yugoslavia's Tito, India's Nehru, Egypt's Nasser, Indonesia's Sukarno, and Ghana's Nkrumah. This summit formally established NAM as an international movement, giving collective voice to nations that refused to join either the American-led NATO bloc or the Soviet-led Warsaw Pact.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe the sequence of events responsible for the establishment of democracy in Nepal.

key_points: Nepal was a Hindu monarchy with the King holding real power
1990 pro-democracy movement forced King to accept constitutional monarchy
Maoist insurgency from 1996 weakened the monarchy
King Gyanendra dismissed government and assumed direct rule in 2005
2006 People's Movement (Jana Andolan II) forced King to restore parliament
2008 Constituent Assembly abolished monarchy and declared Nepal a Federal Democratic Republic

sub_questions.solution: Nepal's transition to democracy was a prolonged and turbulent process shaped by several critical events. Nepal was for long an absolute Hindu monarchy where the King wielded real political power. In 1990, a massive pro-democracy movement forced King Birendra to accept a constitutional monarchy with a multi-party democracy, and a new constitution was enacted. However, democracy remained fragile. From 1996 onwards, the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) launched a violent armed insurgency against the monarchy and the government, plunging the country into civil conflict. King Gyanendra, who ascended the throne after the Royal Palace massacre of 2001, dismissed the elected government in 2005 and assumed direct authoritarian control, suspending democratic rights. This triggered a broad coalition of political parties and civil society groups, who joined hands with the Maoists. In 2006, a massive people's movement — Jana Andolan II — swept the country, forcing King Gyanendra to restore parliament. The restored parliament stripped the King of his powers. In 2008, the Constituent Assembly formally abolished the monarchy and declared Nepal a Federal Democratic Republic, completing the transition from monarchy to democracy.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe the sequence of events responsible for the end of the military government and establishment of democracy in Bangladesh.

key_points: Bangladesh formed in 1971 with Sheikh Mujibur Rahman as first leader
Mujib assassinated in 1975 military coup
General Ziaur Rahman established military rule
Zia assassinated in 1981; General Ershad seized power
Mass movement against Ershad in late 1980s
1990 movement forced Ershad to resign; elections held in 1991 restored parliamentary democracy

sub_questions.solution: Bangladesh's path from military rule to democracy was marked by political instability, coups, and popular resistance. Bangladesh was born in 1971 under Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, who became its first Prime Minister. However, in August 1975, Mujibur Rahman was assassinated in a military coup, and a series of coup attempts followed. General Ziaur Rahman emerged as the dominant leader and established military-backed authoritarian rule, legalising political parties later but maintaining power. After Zia's assassination in 1981, General Hussain Muhammad Ershad seized power in another coup in 1982 and ruled Bangladesh as a military dictator, dissolving parliament and suspending democratic processes. Growing public discontent eventually erupted into a massive pro-democracy movement in the late 1980s. Students, political parties, and civil society groups came together demanding the restoration of democracy. Facing mounting pressure, General Ershad resigned in December 1990. In 1991, free and fair elections were held, and parliamentary democracy was formally restored with Khaleda Zia of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party coming to power. This marked Bangladesh's significant transition from prolonged military rule to elected democratic governance.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the efforts of the Punjab government and the Indian government to foster peace in the State of Punjab.

key_points: Rajiv Gandhi-Longowal Accord (Punjab Accord) of 1985 addressed Akali demands
Operation Blue Star (1984) — military action to flush militants from Golden Temple
Holding fresh elections in Punjab in 1985 after period of President's Rule
Chandrika initiatives and later state police crackdown under K.P.S. Gill restored normalcy by early 1990s

sub_questions.solution: The crisis in Punjab during the 1980s, driven by the Khalistan movement and armed militancy, prompted both the state and central governments to take a series of measures to restore peace. The first major step was Operation Blue Star in June 1984, in which the Indian Army launched a military operation to remove armed militants who had taken refuge in the Golden Temple in Amritsar. This operation succeeded in flushing out the militants but caused significant casualties and damage to the shrine, deepening communal tensions. Following the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and the anti-Sikh riots of 1984, the situation worsened. In 1985, the Rajiv Gandhi government signed the Punjab Accord (also known as the Rajiv-Longowal Accord) with Akali Dal leader Harchand Singh Longowal. This accord addressed long-standing demands such as Chandigarh being given to Punjab, river water disputes, and regional autonomy. Fresh elections were held in Punjab in 1985. However, militancy continued through the late 1980s. The final resolution came through a combination of tough police action under DGP K.P.S. Gill, political initiatives, and the holding of elections in 1992, which helped gradually restore normalcy and democratic governance in Punjab by the mid-1990s.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the main factors responsible for the demands of autonomy by the north-eastern states in India.

key_points: Distinct ethnic, tribal, and cultural identities different from mainland India
Geographical isolation and historical neglect in terms of development
Large-scale migration from Bangladesh and other states altering demographics
Feeling of political and economic marginalisation from central government policies
Colonial legacy of different administrative systems

sub_questions.solution: The demands for autonomy and even independence in India's north-eastern states stem from a complex mix of historical, cultural, geographical, and political factors. First, the region is home to hundreds of distinct ethnic and tribal communities with their own languages, cultures, and traditions that are vastly different from mainstream Indian society. These communities developed a strong sense of separate identity and sought political recognition in the form of separate states or autonomous councils. Second, the geographical isolation of the north-eastern region — connected to mainland India only through the narrow Siliguri Corridor — contributed to a sense of alienation. The region was historically neglected in terms of infrastructure, investment, and economic development, creating deep frustration among the local population. Third, large-scale immigration from Bangladesh and other parts of India into states like Assam and Tripura dramatically altered the demographic composition, triggering fears among indigenous communities about losing their cultural identity, land, and political rights. Fourth, the colonial history of the region, where British administration treated many tribal areas through separate frameworks like the Inner Line Permit system, created a legacy of distinctness that fuelled post-independence demands for continued special status and self-governance.

sub_questions.text_english: How did the Mandal Commission recommendations prove to be an effort to solve the problems of Other Backward Classes (OBCs) ? Analyse.

key_points: Mandal Commission (1979-80) identified OBCs as educationally and socially backward
Recommended 27% reservation in central government jobs for OBCs
Implemented by VP Singh government in 1990
Increased OBC representation in bureaucracy and educational institutions
Politically empowered OBCs and gave voice to their concerns

sub_questions.solution: The Mandal Commission, established in 1979 under the chairmanship of B.P. Mandal, submitted its report in 1980, recommending 27% reservation in central government services and public sector undertakings for Other Backward Classes (OBCs). Its recommendations were implemented in 1990 by the V.P. Singh government, marking a watershed moment in Indian politics and social justice. The commission's recommendations addressed OBC problems in several significant ways. OBCs — comprising castes that were socially and educationally backward but not included in the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe categories — had historically been denied fair representation in government employment and higher education. The 27% reservation provided structured access to these opportunities, enabling first-generation learners from OBC families to enter prestigious government services. This had a transformative effect on social mobility, with many OBC communities gaining a foothold in administrative positions that had long been dominated by upper castes. Beyond material benefits, the implementation of Mandal Commission recommendations had a profound political impact. It galvanised OBCs as a powerful political constituency, making them aware of their rights and encouraging greater participation in electoral politics. Parties began actively courting OBC voters, and OBC leaders rose to prominent positions across states. This political assertion translated into greater sensitivity towards OBC welfare in governance and policymaking.

sub_questions.text_english: Examine any three grounds on which the regional parties support the various coalition governments formed at the Centre in India.

key_points: To gain political influence and secure ministerial positions at the Centre
To extract special economic packages and central funds for their states
To promote state-specific regional interests and get Centre's cooperation on state issues

sub_questions.solution: Regional parties have played a decisive role in supporting coalition governments at the Centre in India, particularly since 1989. Their support is generally based on three key grounds. The first ground is political power and representation. By supporting a coalition government, regional parties secure ministerial positions at the Centre for their leaders, enhancing their political status both nationally and in their home states. This access to central power allows them to influence national policies in ways that benefit their support base. The second ground is economic and developmental benefit for their states. Regional parties use their bargaining power in coalitions to extract special economic packages, increased allocation of central funds, approval of key projects, and relaxation of policies that affect their states' interests. For instance, parties from Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu have historically negotiated significant infrastructure and development grants in exchange for political support. The third ground is the promotion of state-specific interests and autonomy. Regional parties often champion causes related to their state's language, culture, river water disputes, border issues, or demands for greater fiscal autonomy. By being part of or supporting the central government, they gain direct access to decision-making platforms where they can lobby for favourable outcomes on these critical state-level concerns.

sub_questions.text_english: Highlight the differences between the external and internal notions of security in the contemporary world.

key_points: External security deals with threats from other states — war, invasion, nuclear threats
Internal security deals with threats within a country — insurgency, terrorism, civil war, secessionism
External security is managed through military, diplomacy, alliances
Internal security is managed through police, paramilitary, law enforcement, and political dialogue
Distinction is blurring in contemporary world — cross-border terrorism bridges both

sub_questions.solution: In the contemporary world, security is understood through two broad frameworks — external and internal — which, though distinct, are increasingly interconnected. External security refers to threats that originate from outside the state. Traditionally, this meant the threat of military attack or invasion by another country, nuclear threats, or war. To counter external threats, nations rely on military power, diplomatic alliances (such as NATO), deterrence strategies, and international treaties. The army and air force are the primary instruments of external security. Internal security, on the other hand, deals with threats that arise within the country's own borders. These include armed insurgencies, secessionist movements, civil wars, domestic terrorism, ethnic conflicts, and organised crime. For example, India faces internal security threats from Maoist (Naxalite) insurgencies and terrorist activities in Jammu and Kashmir. Internal security is typically managed by the police, paramilitary forces like the CRPF and BSF, intelligence agencies, and political negotiations. A key difference is the level of force used — external threats involve full military engagement, while internal threats require calibrated responses to avoid harming civilians. However, the distinction is increasingly blurred in the modern era. Cross-border terrorism — as seen in the attacks supported from Pakistan — straddles both categories, originating externally but manifesting internally. This has made security management more complex and requires integrated strategies involving both military and civilian agencies.

sub_questions.text_english: "The non-traditional notions of security are more comprehensive than the traditional notions of security." Support the statement with the help of suitable examples.

key_points: Traditional security = military threats between states (war, invasion)
Non-traditional = human security, environmental threats, pandemics, terrorism, food security, economic crises
Non-traditional threats affect millions regardless of state borders
Examples: COVID-19 pandemic, climate change, nuclear terrorism, global food crisis

sub_questions.solution: The traditional notion of security was largely confined to protecting the state from external military threats such as war, invasion, and nuclear strikes. It was state-centric — the primary object of security was the state, and the primary threat was from other states. Non-traditional notions of security are far more comprehensive because they expand both the scope of threats and the subjects whose security needs to be protected. Non-traditional security focuses on human security — the idea that individuals and communities, not just states, must be protected from a wide variety of threats. First, environmental threats such as climate change pose existential risks to millions of people. Rising sea levels threaten the existence of island nations like Maldives, while droughts and extreme weather events displace populations and cause food insecurity — threats no military can directly address. Second, global pandemics like COVID-19 demonstrated how a health crisis can rapidly become a security crisis — killing millions, collapsing economies, and destabilising governments without a single shot being fired. Third, terrorism, including its cross-border and cyber dimensions, poses threats that do not follow state boundaries. The 9/11 attacks showed that non-state actors can cause destruction rivalling conventional war. Fourth, economic crises and food insecurity are increasingly recognised as security threats. The 2008 global financial crisis triggered political instability in multiple countries. These examples show that non-traditional security is more comprehensive because it addresses threats to human life and dignity that conventional military power cannot resolve.
